Añadir un segundo doblete de Higgs es un:
Adding a second Higgs doublet is one of the most natural extensions of the
Standard Model, but it opens the door to scalar-mediated flavor-changing neutral
currents (FCNC) at tree level, which are tightly constrained by experiment. I study
symmetries and flavor structures that keep them under control—or remove them
altogether—in a way that is stable under renormalization group evolution, and how
the new sources of CP violation could have a common origin in the quark and lepton
sectors. These models can also explain the muon and electron anomalous magnetic
moment (g−2) anomalies simultaneously.

La colaboración COMPACT publica en *Natu:
The COMPACT collaboration publishes the article
[“The topology of the Universe”](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-026-02930-6) in
*Nature Astronomy*: is the Universe infinite in all directions? A non-trivial topology
would leave subtle imprints on the cosmic microwave background and on the
three-dimensional distribution of matter, and the article reviews how to look for them
and what upcoming observations will be able to tell.
Los próximos colisionadores electrón–pos:
The next electron–positron colliders (linear or circular, such as CERN's FCC)
will measure the properties of the Higgs boson, the W and Z bosons and the top quark
with unprecedented precision. I work on describing new physics with effective field
theories (SMEFT) and on the constraints these projects will set on top-sector
operators, and I take part in the European studies preparing these machines.

Si el espacio tuviera una topología no t:
If space had a non-trivial topology—that of a torus, for instance—the cosmic
microwave background (CMB) would show characteristic correlations, such as matched
pairs of circles or violations of isotropy and parity. In the COMPACT collaboration
we compute the eigenmodes and correlation matrices of different spaces, study their
detectability and develop machine learning techniques to recognize the shape of the
Universe.

Soy físico teórico de partículas (fenome:
I am a theoretical particle physicist (phenomenology) in the Department of Physics
at the University of Córdoba, where I am a member of the
[FQM-429](https://www.uco.es/investiga/grupos/acp/) research group. I work on
**flavor** physics and **CP** violation in two-Higgs-doublet models, on the anomalous
magnetic moments of leptons (**g−2**), and on what **future colliders** can tell us
about the top quark and the Higgs boson.

I am also interested in cosmology: in the **COMPACT** collaboration we search for the
**topology of the Universe** in the cosmic microwave background, with the help of
machine learning.
